title: Client graceful failover: priority preservation and partial draft archival
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Problem: Long-running streaming generations are vulnerable to client disconnects, flaky mobile SDKs, and transient network partitions. When clients drop, partial generations (draft text, KV cache, in-flight function/tool calls) can either be lost (causing user-visible regressions) or retained indefinitely (consuming GPU memory and storage). Current strategies either aggressively GC partial drafts (causes UX/consistency issues) or conservatively keep them (costly, leads to orphaned state).

Goal: Implement an adaptive failover and archival strategy that: preserves user-priority drafts (recent/high-urgency streams) for a longer grace window, opportunistically archives low-priority partial drafts to object storage for later resumption, reconciles KV cache and tool-call state on resume, and exposes clear SLOs/metrics for partial-generation cleanup and resumption success. Keep the design compatible with older SDK versions and hosted/dedicated/private deployments.

Scope (in this ticket):
- Lease/priority annotations for streaming generations (metadata on creation: priority=P0|P1|P2).
- Adaptive grace window: base TTL + priority multiplier + heuristic extension for recent activity.
- Tiered cleanup: in-memory retention -> soft-archive (fast cold storage, resumable) -> hard-delete.
- Archive format: compacted draft + KV delta + tool-call checkpoint (JSONL), with metadata about SDK version and model variant.
- Resume protocol: handshake that validates archive fingerprint, reconciles KV cache differences, replays pending tool calls if idempotent or marks as retried.
- Backpressure integration: server-side signals to downstream runtime to reduce batch aggregation for clients flagged as unstable.
- SDK compatibility shim: older SDKs will fall back to conservative behavior (shorter resume hints) and be routed to a compatibility layer.

Out-of-scope: full rework of rollout policies, dedicated capacity autoscaling rules (separate project), and cross-region archival replication.

Why this approach: Balances UX (users can often resume interrupted compositions) with operational cost (archived drafts are cheaper than live memory/epoch queues). Priority multipliers let product teams tune retention for high-value flows (billing receipts, legal transcripts) vs ephemeral chat. Archival format keeps resume simple and model-agnostic.
acceptance_criteria: Server maintains per-generation priority metadata and uses it to compute adaptive grace windows
Partial generations transition through retention -> soft-archive -> hard-delete within configured schedules
Resume flow can restore an archived generation with >=95% reconstruction success for KV cache keys within the same model family
No regression in steady-state GPU memory usage (<=5% increase over baseline) after feature flag rollout to 10% traffic
Instrumented metrics in Console: orphaned_generation_count, archived_generation_count, resume_success_rate, average_grace_window_by_priority
tasks: Design RFC for lease/priority metadata and archive format (link in links)
Implement server-side priority annotation and adaptive TTL computation
Implement soft-archive writer and small-object compaction job
Add resume handshake logic and KV reconciliation heuristics
Expose metrics and dashboard in Console; add alert for orphaned_generations_rate > 0.5%
Write SDK compatibility shim and e2e tests for resume across SDK versions
Roll out behind feature flag to 10% runtime traffic, monitor for 72h, then 50%
decisions: Use three-tier lifecycle (in-memory -> soft-archive -> hard-delete) to minimize live memory pressure
Archive format will be JSONL containing compacted tokens + key-deltas + tool-call checkpoints to keep cross-language compatibility
Tool-call replay will be attempted only for idempotent calls; non-idempotent calls will be marked and surfaced in resume metadata for client reconciliation
Compatibility mode for older SDKs will expose resumability hints but require explicit opt-in from SDK upgrade to enable automatic resume
